title: HandyX
summary: A marketplace of home-service specialists in Mar del Plata: residents ask for a repair from their phone, get proposals with an itemised price and choose. Ahead of launch, a landing page collects the waiting list, a purpose-built backend stores every pre-registration encrypted and an internal portal works it through a contact funnel.

facts.v: Sole person: product, design and development
Landing with demo · backend · internal portal

tldr.v: When something breaks at home you don't know what it will cost, extras appear without warning and you end up handing out your phone number.
Proposals with an itemised price, nothing extra without your OK, and the specialist sets the price. The fee is shown before you confirm.
Landing, backend and portal built and tested locally. Launches on Nov 10; no users or metrics yet.

p: Handyx connects Mar del Plata residents with independent home-service specialists. It starts with six trades: electrical, plumbing, gas, locksmith, masonry and air conditioning.
list: Resident: asks for a repair (urgent, scheduled or a bigger job), gets clear proposals and chooses. The total they see is what they pay.
Specialist: receives requests, sets their own price (Handyx only suggests a reference) and is paid straight into their account. No exclusivity and no penalty for declining.
Operations: before launch, an internal portal sorts out who to message, what stage each specialist is at and who to notify.

p: Installing and signing up are free. Handyx charges a 10 % fee to the person who asks and 10 % to the specialist, on every job done. The money for the job goes to the specialist's account; Handyx only charges its fee, which is shown before confirming.
money.title: How a $45,000 job is split
money.caption: Example with the sample quote from the landing page (Argentine pesos). The fee collection mechanism is not built yet.

p: The landing page has a single goal: real pre-registrations. Everything else serves that, with no tricks.

items.d: «I want to use Handyx» (waiting list) and «I'm a specialist» (pre-registration), each with its own page.
A panel with a QR code generated in the browser, a link and WhatsApp. No referral codes or tracking parameters.
The public counter only appears from 20 sign-ups and rounds down in steps of 5: never an inflated number.

items.t: A demo to show in person
items.d: The app for both roles with fictional data, with a looping «stand» mode for events.

p: A pre-registration is not an account or a verified specialist: it is someone to get in touch with. The portal works it as a state machine with rules on the server, and opening WhatsApp is always a person's click.

diagram.title: From pre-registration to commitment
diagram.caption: States stored in the backend. Every change travels with the version the operator saw and an idempotency key, and is applied in one transaction with its audit record.

pre.label: Pre-registered
pre.note: Each unanswered attempt adds one, but doesn't change the state.

commit.label: Committed
commit.note: Requires a start date within the next 90 days.

told.label: Notified
told.note: Only people from Mar del Plata are notified, since that's where it starts.

p: Three pieces of my own: a static landing page, a backend that serves both the public capture and the internal CRM, and a portal for the team. The browser never touches the database: everything goes through the API.

diagram.title: The system, end to end
diagram.caption: Planned hosting: Hostinger for the websites, Render for the API and Neon for PostgreSQL. Nothing is deployed or contracted yet.

api.label: API and CRM
api.note: One API for the public capture and for the team, with separate CORS.

db.label: PostgreSQL
db.note: Name, WhatsApp, city and email are stored encrypted; never in plain text.

portal.label: Internal portal
portal.note: Session in HttpOnly cookies; nothing is stored in the browser.

p: Sign-up is the only moment personal data comes in, so it is the most careful flow. The same schema validates in the browser and on the server, and a duplicate gets exactly the same answer as a new sign-up, so nobody can find out who has signed up.

seq.title: From the form to the database
seq.caption: If the database fails the answer is 503: never a false success. The landing page only shows success on a 201.

p: There is personal data from day one, so privacy was designed before the screens.

items.d: AES-256-GCM with the row and column as authenticated data; duplicates are detected with an HMAC under a different key.
A duplicate gets the same answer as a sign-up and the public counter is a lower bound: you can't tell whether someone signed up.
Argon2id passwords, a TOTP second factor for accounts that have one, HttpOnly cookies, CSRF and exact Origin. Accounts live in the server's environment: no sign-up and no admin table.
Each endpoint requires a permission from a closed list, and reading a record is audited before the answer goes out.
An allow-list of fields: never bodies, cookies, SQL queries or personal values.
Every pre-registration expires after 12 months and is really deleted, with a procedure for data-subject rights.

items.t: One contract, copied byte for byte
items.why: The landing page and the API validate with the same schema, and a test checks that both files are identical. The browser and the server can't drift apart.
An exact public number would let anyone test whether a person had signed up: send their contact and watch it go up.
With no sign-up and no admin table there is nothing to attack on that side, and removing someone takes effect on the next request, without a restart.
The landing page is a static multi-page site generated at build time from JSON; the portal is a light SPA, chosen as a reversible option while the app's stack is decided.
items.alt: React for the portal: still open until the app's stack is decided.

items.t: Capture closed until the final notice
items.why: No personal data is collected under a provisional privacy notice: the landing page says «Sign-up opens soon» and the API answers 503.
Sessions and limits in memory, for a bounded four-phase scope. The accepted cost: a restart means signing in again.

p: All three repos have type checks and CI. The backend also runs lint, formatting, npm audit and an ephemeral PostgreSQL database on every PR.

items.d: Landing: money, dates, schedule, proposals, schema and links
Backend against PostgreSQL: encryption, concurrency, privileges and purge
Portal: session, contract, rules and permissions

quality.note: I ran the landing, backend (unit and HTTP) and portal tests on 10/28/2026: all green. I listed the 64 database tests; they need PostgreSQL and run in CI.

status.h: Status, and what I don't claim
list: In development. The launch is planned for November 10, 2026 in Mar del Plata.
Nothing is deployed and there is no real data: no users, sign-ups or metrics to show.
A pre-registered specialist is not verified: verification isn't built yet.
There are no payments and no mobile app in these repos. HandIA, in the demo, is a scripted chat, not an AI model.
I'm the only person on the project: product, design and development.
